matchups.analysis: Ben's walking out of here at 100% with ESPN calling this finished, and Rob's sitting at 96.5 watching the scoreboard with absolutely nothing left to play—the gap's 19.4 points and it's locked in stone. Rob's lineup card was a fucking disaster though: he benched Kyle Pitts Sr. for Christian Kirk and watched Kirk put up a fat goose egg while Pitts was chilling on the bench with 10.7 points, which is exactly the kind of self-own that haunts you when you're already getting murdered. Meanwhile Ben caught lightning with Caleb Douglas (20.0 vs 5.6 projected) and survived Justin Jefferson turning into a ghost act (6.4 vs 15.4 projected), then made the insane decision to bench Malachi Fields for DeMario Douglas—but honestly it doesn't matter because Jameson Williams going nuclear for Rob (23.6 vs 8.9) just got completely swallowed by Garrett Wilson's flatline and those benching blunders. This one's been dead for hours; Rob just benched his way out of making it interesting.

Nori's staring at a 1% lifeline while Veton's already counting his chips at 99%—ESPN's got this locked down with a 37.9-point gap and only Javonte Williams left to chip away at it, which is basically asking a running back to score more than an entire competent lineup. The real damage was benching Marvin Harrison Jr. (7.1) for Jaylin Noel (0.7) when you were already chasing a blowout, but let's be honest: that 6.4-point mistake barely registers when Jahmyr Gibbs completely no-showed his assignment and left 8.7 points on the field. Veton didn't even need to gameplan—just rode Tony Pollard's 35.0-point explosion (projected 12.9) to the finish line while everything else fell into place, and now you're hoping Javonte does the impossible instead of whatever the hell Gibbs did all day.

Arben's walking away with this one at 100% with ESPN locking in 113.6 to Faton's 109.0—a 4.6-point gap that's already sealed since you both finished your lineups. The real damage for Faton was benching Blake Corum (16.6 pts) to start Chuba Hubbard (8.0 pts), which is exactly the kind of decision that loses close matchups when you're already spotting someone nearly 5 points to begin with—that 8.6-point swing cost you the entire week right there. Jaxon Smith-Njigba demolished his projection for Arben (26.8 vs 16.3) while your best play was Bo Nix outrunning his own ceiling, but none of that matters when you're starting the wrong running back and watching it sink you.

Flamur's running away with this at 93% with ESPN projecting 97.5 to Ilir's 74.9—that's a 22.6-point gap that basically locks in the moment CeeDee Lamb and Saquon Barkley check in, assuming they show up and do literally anything. Ilir's entire path to relevance depends on George Pickens going absolutely unhinged, but the real execution failure was benching Omar Cooper Jr. (20.0 points) to start Jalen Coker (1.4)—that's an 18.6-point swing that single-handedly turned a close matchup into a blowout before the weekend even started. Tee Higgins demolished his projection by 12 points and proved competent roster decisions exist, while Ilir's watching Isaiah Likely crater and Jalen Coker prove he had zero business eating a starting slot—this one's already dead, Pickens would just be consolation prize territory at this point.

Rinor's getting absolutely demolished here—down 20.5 points with only Dak left to play while Jetmir's already locked in at 98.1 with ESPN calling this 70-30 in his favor, and honestly that's being generous to you. The real damage was benching Devaughn Vele (13.9 pts) for Aaron Jones Sr. (3.1 pts)—that's a 10.8-point swing you'll be thinking about all week—but then Derrick Henry decided to completely no-show at 5.4 when ESPN had him at 17.4, which means you've basically already handed this one away before Dak even steps on the field. Jetmir's got the cleaner roster that didn't require any miracles; he won this one when he avoided the trap of overthinking his lineup, and you lost it the moment you convinced yourself benching your best option for one of the worst performers on your bench was a smart play. Bucky Irving going off for 23.5 is your only bright spot, but one guy overperforming can't save you when you've actively sabotaged yourself on both your lineup decisions.

Adam's cruising at 99% with ESPN projecting a clean 111.5 finish while Rilind's stuck at 85.7 with only Darius Cooper left to play—basically needing a 26-point explosion from a single guy just to tie, and that's being generous about how much help he's getting. The real story here is how badly Rilind torpedoed himself by benching Dalton Schultz (7.0) to start Konata Mumpfield (2.0), which cost him 5 points he absolutely couldn't afford to lose when he's already chasing ghosts. Adam's Zay Flowers absolutely demolished his projection at 23.7 (projected 12.0) and carried the load even though Xavier Worthy completely shit the bed at 2.6—but when your floor is this high you can absorb that kind of underperformance and still walk away untouched. Rilind's Denzel Boston also underperformed projection by 6 points, but the bench-sitting decision is what actually killed this thing before Cooper even steps on the field.
